_about: Altitude bands, bottom to top (scripts/sim/sim_rules.gd reads this; unit files name the bands they may use). ALL PROPOSED by Track S, 2026-10-09. The design doc's unit sheet asks for a 'height layer or altitude band' per unit and says height limits sight lines and engagement and that diving adds speed and can hide a plane behind mountains; it does not say how many bands there are or how high. The demo flies every plane in one band (Alex: altitude may be a fixed band for now), but the data shape carries it so shadows and, later, line of sight can use it.
_rules: LIST ORDER IS VERTICAL ORDER: a climb is a move to a later entry, a dive to an earlier one. reference 'terrain' = the height is above the ground under the unit (ground and sea units ride the surface); 'sea_level' = an absolute height, so a ridge taller than the band can hide a plane. Cross-track constraint (proposed): Track T's highest terrain level plus its tallest trees must stay below the lowest air band, since the sim has no terrain collision yet.

height_m._reason: ground and sea units sit on whatever surface is under them; Track T's height_at(x, y) gives the actual height
nap of the earth: low enough that a hill or ridge can hide the plane (design doc, Height), above the trees
above an island's ordinary terrain, inside light anti-aircraft range; the demo's fixed band
above the island's tallest mountains, the band a bomber holds over defended targets
